Fixes alkem-io/server#6775

This PR is the `/bugfix` record for the issue above. It has no workspace spec.

## Root cause

The server sends an actor's display name to Matrix (`communicationAdapter.syncActor`) in only three places:
- user creation (`user.service.ts:287`)
- VC creation (`virtual.contributor.service.ts:209`)
- the platform-admin bulk resync (`admin.communication.space.sync.service.ts:513,527`)

No update path calls it. When someone renames a user or a VC, Matrix keeps the old name, so Element Call tiles and room membership show it.

## Every path that changes an actor's `profile.displayName`

All of them end in `ProfileService.updateProfile` (`src/domain/common/profile/profile.service.ts`):
- `UserService.updateUser` → `profileService.updateProfile` (`user.service.ts:1176`). Used by the client-web settings profile tab and the admin user page.
- `VirtualContributorService.updateVirtualContributor` → `profileService.updateProfile` (`virtual.contributor.service.ts:314`).
- The generic `updateProfile` mutation → `profileService.updateProfile` (`profile.resolver.mutations.ts:118`). It can target any profile, including a user's or a VC's.

No other code writes a user's or VC's `profile.displayName` after creation. The other `profile.displayName =` writes are creation-time defaults (`user.identity.service.ts:312`, `virtual.contributor.defaults.service.ts:54`) or belong to non-actor profiles (`user-group.service.ts:123`). Organizations are never synced to Matrix: `syncActor` is called only for users and VCs. Renaming an organization therefore stays unsynced.

## Fix

The sync lives in the owner every path shares, `ProfileService.updateProfile`. Fixing it per entry point would leave the generic mutation uncovered.
- The service records the display name before applying the input. After saving, it acts only if the name **actually changed** and the profile type is `USER` or `VIRTUAL_CONTRIBUTOR`. Every other profile update costs nothing extra.
- The profile type alone does not give the actor id or `nameID`, so the service looks up the owning actor with one query on the actor table's unique `profileId` join column (`Actor.findOne`, selecting `id` and `nameID`). This runs only on a real rename.
- The name comes from `getActorDisplayName`, the same formula creation and the bulk resync use, so the trimmed `displayName` falls back to `nameID`.
- `ProfileModule` now imports `CommunicationAdapterModule`. That module depends only on the global RPC module, so this adds no import cycle.

What was copied from `createUser`, and why:
- **Awaited `syncActor` inside try/catch, log and never throw. Kept.** The rename is already saved when the sync runs, so a Matrix outage must not turn a successful save into an error. Awaiting keeps the failure inside this try/catch, which avoids an unhandled rejection. The RPC timeout bounds the wait, and only real renames pay it.
- **Not copied: the avatar.** `createUser` passes no avatar, and matrix-adapter's `SetUserProfile` skips an empty avatar. Passing none therefore changes only the name.
- **Added beyond `createUser`:** `syncActor` returns `false` when the adapter answers without success. This change logs a warning in that case instead of ignoring it.
- **Not handled: an update whose actor lookup finds nothing.** The service logs a warning and skips the sync.

matrix-adapter's `SyncActor` is idempotent (EnsureUser, then SetUserProfile), so the fix needs no adapter change.

## Regression test

New tests in `src/domain/common/profile/profile.service.spec.ts` (`updateProfile - Matrix display name sync`). They call the real `ProfileService.updateProfile`. Only the persistence boundary (`Profile.findOne`, `Actor.findOne`, repository save) and the `CommunicationAdapter` are stubbed. The cases:
- a renamed user is synced **once**, with the new name, for the actor that owns the profile
- a renamed VC is synced
- an unchanged display name is **not** synced, and no actor lookup runs
- an update with no `displayName` is not synced
- an organization rename is not synced
- a blank name falls back to `nameID`
- if the sync throws, or the adapter reports failure, the updated profile is still returned
- if no actor owns the profile, nothing is synced

I checked that the tests fail without the fix: with the sync call disabled, the 4 positive cases fail.

Gates: `pnpm lint` (tsc + biome), `pnpm build` and `pnpm test:ci:no:coverage` (924 files / 12468 tests) all pass. A manual `new ProfileService(...)` in `test/integration/content-signing/signing-attempt.postgres.spec.ts` got the extra constructor argument.

The new comments describe behaviour only. They carry no spec or issue references, per `docs/conventions/code-comments.md`.

## Operator follow-up

This fix only affects renames made after it deploys. Names that went stale before then stay stale until the user or VC is renamed again, or a platform admin runs the bulk communication sync (`AdminCommunicationSpaceSyncService.syncDisplayNames`). Run it once after deploying.

## Summary

Data repair for space roles whose `credential.resourceID` points at a **different space**. Cause: `RoleService.createRole` aliased the module-level role definitions, and `updateRoleResourceID` mutated them in place during recursive template-subspace creation. efb6d8ea8 (#6467) fixed this for new data only. On acceptance: 162 roles on 54 spaces, 167 issued credentials, and 6,414 stored policies that grant one space's privileges to members of another.

```text
up()                                    (one transaction, every change logged)
  1. role.credential.resourceID := owning space id               162 roles
  2. for each credential (type, wrong target) issued via those roles
       owner evidence  = member-joined in owner within 60s | invitation/application on owner
       target evidence = same tests against the target
       owner evidence              -> grant (type, owner) if missing   164
       owner && !target evidence   -> revoke (type, target)            163
         except membership kept if holder is in a subspace of target     1
       target space deleted        -> revoke
       no evidence either way      -> untouched, logged 'ambiguous'      0
  3. space-subspace-admin re-derived for the owners                18 moved
  4. parentCredentials recomputed in the owners' subtrees          420 roles
  5. any mis-pointed role left -> throw (rollback)
down()  replays _repair_mispointed_role_credentials in reverse
```

**Post-deploy (required):** run `mutation { authorizationPolicyResetAll }` and let it drain, because stored policies keep the old grants until the reset. Flush the role-set membership cache, or wait for `collaboration.membership.cache_ttl` (4h).

Run on a restored copy of the acceptance DB (2026-11-04), measured with the data-consistency suite (1,149 read-only checks):

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `auth-role-space-resourceid-mismatch` | 162 | 0 |
| `…mispointed-role-creds-issued` | 167 | 0 |
| `…mispointed-role-creds-holder-without-owner-cred` | 164 | 0 |
| `…space-policies-crit-from-mispointed-role` | 6,414 | 0 |
| `…space-l2-role-parentcredentials-missing-l0` | 464 | 74 (outside the affected subtrees) |

- No check errors, and nothing changes outside the role and credential domains.

- `up()` takes 0.5 s. A second `up()` is a no-op.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Every change is logged, and `migration:revert` restores the exact prior rows. The policies are recomputed by the reset either way.

**Blast Radius:** authorization

Refs #6614. Split out of #6637, which keeps the delete-path fixes. This PR is only the one-off cleanup of the orphans those leaks left behind.

## Migration — `1790800000000-CleanUpOrphanedRecordsAndPolicies`

One-off and **reversible**. It deletes, in this order:
1. classifications, licenses and profiles that nothing names; their cascading children go with them;
2. the locations and storage buckets owned by the profiles deleted in step 1;
3. every authorization policy that nothing names, including the ones freed by steps 1–2.

Policies go last on purpose. The issue allows any order, and going last also catches the policies that steps 1–2 free.

### Backups and `down()`

Every deleted row is copied whole into `_orphan_cleanup_backup_<table>`. The copy happens in the same SQL statement as the delete, and every part of that statement reads the database as it was before any row is deleted. Three things are copied:
- the row itself;
- the children Postgres deletes with it (tagset, reference, visual, license_entitlement);
- every reference to it that Postgres sets to NULL, kept in `_orphan_cleanup_backup_nulled_references`. Today the only such reference is `file.tagsetId`.

The backups stay in place until the fix is confirmed. `down()` then inserts the rows back parents first, restores each nulled reference that is **still NULL** (one that was set since is left alone), and drops the backup tables.

The backup tables are not counted as names, otherwise the copies would keep the rows they copy. If a table is backed up but missing from `RESTORE_ORDER`, `up()` throws, so `down()` can never silently skip a backup.

**Follow-up:** once the fix is confirmed, a later migration drops the `_orphan_cleanup_backup_*` tables. Only `down()` drops them today.

### Safeguards
- **A row is kept while anything names it:** any foreign key, or any column carrying its id under the conventional name. The migration backup tables, e.g. `_auth_profile_backup_*.profileId`, hold such columns without an FK. Only an explicit list of each table's own cascading children is ignored, so an unknown reference keeps the row, including an owner whose key cascades. If nothing names a table at all, the migration throws instead of deleting every row.
- **There is no generic bucket or location sweep.** The Matrix media staging bucket is named only from configuration (`storage.file_service.matrix_media_bucket_id`). Only buckets and locations whose profile this migration deleted are removed.
- **Files are never deleted.** Their content lives in file-service storage, which only file-service may release. An unowned profile whose bucket holds files is left whole and counted in the log.
- **Rows created in the last day are skipped,** so an in-flight create, which saves children before their parent, cannot lose a child.
- **Only deleted ids come back to Node** (plus a deleted profile's location and bucket ids). Whole rows go from the delete straight into the backup inside Postgres, so ~15k policies' rule JSON is never held in Node memory.

## Dry run on a full dev copy of acceptance data (`up()` → `down()`, rolled back)

| | deleted | after `down()` |
|---|---|---|
| classifications | 2,997 | byte-identical |
| licenses / entitlements | 12 / 106 | byte-identical |
| profiles / locations / storage buckets | 44 / 44 / 44 | byte-identical |
| tagsets / references / visuals | 2,918 / 25 / 13 | byte-identical |
| authorization policies | 15,396 | byte-identical |
| files | 0 | byte-identical |

`up()` took ~14 s. A second run deletes nothing. 12 unowned profile trees whose buckets hold files are left for a file-service cleanup.

Of the deleted classifications, 729 are the live leak since April; the rest are 2025 rows whose policy was never computed, with no owner.

## Tests
- `clean-up-orphaned-records-and-policies.postgres.spec.ts` (10 cases) runs in the CI PostgreSQL job via `pnpm run test:migration:orphan-cleanup:postgres`, which fails rather than skips when `MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. One case runs `up()` then `down()` and expects every table to come back byte-identical, including a nulled `file.tagsetId`. Removing any one safeguard turns a specific case red; so do dropping the nulled-reference capture and dropping the backup-table exclusion.

## Deploy notes
- Rollback: `migration:revert` restores the deleted rows from the backup tables. The deploy pipeline's gated pre-migration backup remains the last resort.
- Independent of #6637 in either order. Until #6637 ships, the delete paths keep leaking, so some orphans will reappear after this runs.

## Not in this PR
- The policy leaks of the group-A delete paths and failed creates.
- File-bearing orphan trees, historical empty orphan buckets (the 813 in the issue), and orphaned aggregators/documents: these need a file-service path.
- Dropping the backup tables (follow-up, above).

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. Existing drifted spaces (acceptance, where QA reproduced this) are healed on deploy.

- `innovation.flow.service.spec.ts` — add-state (incl. sort-order insertion) and delete-state (incl. deleting the current state) rewrite the vocabulary with the shared default rule; two pins for the default rule on the template path.
- `tagset.service.spec.ts` — rename branch saves the re-tagged tagset.
- `src/migrations/__tests__/1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates.spec.ts` — structural pins (three ordered UPDATEs, idempotence guards, case-insensitive re-tag, no DDL, no-op down).
- #6339's transfer pins (`classification.service.spec.ts`, `callout.transfer.service.spec.ts`) unchanged and green.

Fixes alkem-io/server#6492

## Root cause

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. The renderer correctly fails rather than silently changing the signed output, but the existing collaboration migration worker had no memo-image discovery or repair path.

## Fix

- extends the existing one-shot collaboration migration worker with `--repair-memo-images --actor-id <uuid>`; it is a read-only dry run by default, and mutation requires explicit `--apply`
- reads each current memo through the live collaboration room, reports exact missing references and repeated occurrence counts, and only treats typed metadata absence or a typed file-service 404 as confirmed loss
- leaves authorization failures, transport failures/timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed responses, foreign-bucket metadata, and malformed internal locators untouched and reports the memo as failed
- removes only confirmed-missing image nodes from the fresh live Yjs document and persists via the existing correlated durability-barrier path, so concurrent edits are not overwritten by a stale snapshot
- preserves valid/external images and unrelated memo text, formatting, lists, and tables; rerunning a completed repair is a no-op
- reports visual loss explicitly, while the repaired projection is also the projection used by preview/signing

The memo image schema contains no alternate byte source to recover a genuinely absent internal document. Images whose metadata and non-empty file-service bytes are available are preserved.

## Tests

- focused repair/CLI/module suite: 18 passed
- full `pnpm test:ci`: 793 files passed, 8 skipped; 9,247 tests passed, 28 skipped
- `pnpm build`: passed
- `pnpm lint` (TypeScript + Biome): passed
- commit hooks: full no-coverage test suite and typecheck passed

No production or acceptance repair was executed. No memo, file, signing attempt, or external environment was mutated while implementing or testing this PR.

## Bug
Using **Message** from inside a modal dialog (the callout dialog, the expanded contributor map, or a comment's hover card inside the callout dialog) opened the chat **behind** the dialog's overlay, and the chat was unusable:
- you could not click into it (the dialog sets `pointer-events: none` on `<body>`);
- the composer could not keep focus (the dialog's focus trap pulled it back);
- screen readers could not see it (the dialog marks the rest of the page `aria-hidden`);
- the mouse wheel could not scroll the thread (the dialog's scroll lock cancels wheel/touch outside it);
- pressing inside it dismissed the dialog underneath.

## Root cause
`ChatPanel` was a plain fixed `div` rendered in the app tree. It took no part in the Radix layer stack, so an open Radix modal treated it as "outside" for every one of its page locks.

## Fix
The chat now floats above an open dialog and stays usable (product decision: the dialog stays open behind the chat). All of it is in the one shared shell, `ChatPanel`:
- **portalled to the end of `<body>`**: it paints above an already-open dialog, and it is outside the siblings that dialog marked `aria-hidden`;
- **`DismissableLayerBranch`**: presses and focus inside the chat do not dismiss open Radix layers;
- **`FocusScope`** (non-trapped): pauses the dialog's focus trap, the same mechanism `AssistantPanelContent` already uses;
- **`RemoveScroll`** (`noIsolation`, no scrollbar removal): becomes the active scroll lock, so the chat scrolls and the page is not newly locked;
- **`pointer-events-auto`** on the panel and its backdrop.

A dialog opened *after* the chat still covers it, as any modal covers the page. For the case where the chat is already open, then a dialog opens over it, then Message is clicked inside that dialog: `UserMessagingContext` now counts open requests, and `UnifiedChatLauncher` keys the panel connector on that count. Each request remounts the panel back on top. The only local state lost is the panel's expanded toggle, and Message navigates to a thread anyway.

`@radix-ui/react-dismissable-layer@1.1.11` and `react-remove-scroll@2.7.2` are added as direct dependencies, pinned to the exact versions Radix already resolves. Their layer and lock stacks are module-level, so the chat must share the same copy as the dialogs. This is the same reason `@radix-ui/react-focus-scope` is pinned. The lockfile only adds these two entries.

## Regression tests
- `ChatPanel.modal.test.tsx` renders a real Radix `Dialog` with the chat opened from inside it. It asserts the chat is not `aria-hidden` and is stacked after the dialog, gets pointer events, keeps composer focus, does not dismiss the dialog on pointer-down, and is not wheel-blocked. It also covers the chat-already-open case: a dialog covers the chat, and a new open request brings it back above. All 6 fail on `develop`, each on its own assertion.
- `UnifiedChatLauncher.test.tsx`: the panel remounts for every open request, including one made while it is open. This test fails without the `key`.
- `ChatPanel.test.tsx`: the backdrop lookups use `document` because the panel is now portalled.

Gates: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm vitest run` (703 files, 6150 tests), `pnpm build` are all green.

**Not live-verified:** the local backend was down at verification time (Traefik returned 502 for every app route). Unit coverage runs in jsdom, which has no real paint order or hit-testing. The expanded-map path is covered only through the shared `ChatPanel` path.

## Root cause
`ContributorMap`'s pin popup could only render what `ContributorMapPin` carries: avatar, name and role. `ContributorCollection` built the pins from the full `ContributorCardData` and dropped every other card field. So people who share a location got less on the map than unlocated people got in the list. The inline map and the expanded-map dialog both render the same `ContributorMap`, so both had the gap. The only other consumer is the admin view-capture map in `FramingEditorConnector`, which keeps today's name-only popup.

## Fix
- **`ContributorMap`** has a new optional `renderPinCard(pinId)` slot. When the slot is set, the popup shows its content, and the map still never imports callout code. The popup:
  - is a labelled non-modal dialog (`aria-label` = the contributor's name) and gets focus when it opens;
  - closes on Esc or with a close button (reuses the existing `crd-common` `close` string, so no new i18n keys), and both return focus to the pin that opened it;
  - is capped at `min(20rem, 100vw - 2rem)` wide, which overrides maplibre's 240px `maxWidth` default;
  - is capped at `min(18rem, 60vh)` tall and scrolls inside;
  - has per-anchor offsets so it never covers the avatar, and maplibre picks the side that fits in the small h-96 map.
- **`ContributorCollection`** fills the slot with the same `ContributorCard` the list uses, built from the `filtered` data it already has (no new queries). This covers users and organisations, with Message whenever `onMessage` and `canMessage` allow it. It does this for both the inline and the expanded map. The expanded-map `DialogContent` ignores an Esc that comes from inside the popup (`onEscapeKeyDown` + `preventDefault`), so Esc closes the popup and not the whole map.
- When no slot is passed, the popup is unchanged.

### Why the Message menu works inside the popup (checked against the library source)
- maplibre attaches popups to `map.getContainer()`, but its pan/zoom/click handlers listen on `map.getCanvasContainer()` (maplibre-gl 5.24 `popup.ts` / `handler_manager.ts`). Pointer and key events inside the popup therefore never reach the map, so they can't pan it or close the popup.
- The Radix dropdown is portalled to `body` at `z-50` and mounts after the dialog, so it shows above the expanded-map dialog. Radix treats it as a nested layer, so the dialog doesn't block clicks on it.
- The popup's Esc handler ignores keys from portalled content, so Esc inside an open "…" menu closes only the menu.

## Regression test
`src/crd/components/callout/ContributorCollection/ContributorCollection.map.test.tsx` renders the real `ContributorCollection` → lazy `ContributorMap` path. Only the WebGL `react-map-gl/maplibre` layer is replaced with plain DOM stand-ins. It checks that:
- a user pin shows the full card (tagline, tags, location, role) and that Message calls `onMessage`;
- an organisation pin shows the full card (associates, website link, actions menu);
- Esc closes the popup and focus returns to the pin;
- the close button does the same;
- on the expanded map, the pin shows the full card, Esc closes only the popup, the expanded dialog stays open and focus returns to the pin.

**RED confirmed:** all 5 tests failed against unmodified `develop` (the popup had no card). I also removed the expanded-map Esc guard as a check, and the expanded-map test failed without it.

- `pnpm vitest run`: 684 files, 5985 passed / 4 skipped
- `pnpm build`: pass
- `pnpm lint` (tsc + biome ci + eslint): pass

The new code comments carry no spec, issue or PR references.

## Problem

In a direct conversation whose Matrix room is end-to-end encrypted, pressing Send shows "Send was not confirmed. Check the conversation before sending again." and no request leaves the browser.

The browser Matrix client runs without crypto. For a room that carries an `m.room.encryption` state event, matrix-js-sdk throws before making any HTTP call:

```
Error sending event Error: This room is configured to use encryption, but your client does not support encryption.
    at encryptEventIfNeeded
```

`handleSendMessage` swallows that error and returns `false`, so nothing reaches Synapse, the server logs or APM. Alkemio's own rooms are not encrypted; the affected rooms were encrypted outside Alkemio and encryption cannot be turned off again in Matrix.

## Change

Before a text send, `useConversationView` checks `room.hasEncryptionStateEvent()`. For an encrypted room the text goes through the existing `sendMessageToRoom` mutation (the path attachments already use) instead of straight to Synapse. Unencrypted rooms are unchanged.

The mutation applies the same checks server-side: `CREATE_MESSAGE` on the room and, for direct conversations, the recipient's "allow messages" setting.

## Notes for review

- A message sent this way is stored unencrypted in a room marked as encrypted. Other Matrix clients may flag it as unencrypted.
- Not exercised against a real encrypted room yet; covered by a unit test only.
- Out of scope: other send failures are still swallowed without a specific message or an APM report.

## Testing

- New unit test: a text send into an encrypted room calls `sendMessageToRoom` and makes no direct Synapse call.
- Full pre-commit suite passes (lint, `tsc`, vitest).

## What / why

Rotates a non-refreshable Matrix credential that is 40 h old when a call click finds it due; that click opens nothing, and the call buttons return once the new session syncs. Requests no refresh token and lengthens no credential's life (workspace#102).

Synapse ends every non-refreshable session at 48 h (`session_lifetime`), which drops any call running at that moment. The refresh-token fix for minted sessions was declined (it would stretch a stolen token from 48 h to up to 30 days). This PR instead swaps a near-expiry credential at the one safe moment — before a call starts — and logs the old token out early.

- **`storage.ts` / `mintSession.ts` / `matrixCallback.ts`** — both credential writers stamp `issuedAt`; a record without it counts as due.
- **`ssoLogin.ts`** — `attemptSilentSso({ replacing })`: the record of the device being replaced is not taken as success.
- **`sessionController.ts`** — `rotateIfDue()`: one attempt per record, one rotation at a time. It takes over another tab's newer record, otherwise acquires (silent SSO, then mint; never clears storage first), then stops the old client, fires a best-effort `POST /_matrix/client/v3/logout` with the old token, and starts the new one with the chat marked as connecting. `recover()` clears the stored record only when it is the rejected device's (cross-tab).
- **`activeSession.ts`** — `rotateActiveSessionIfDue(): Promise<boolean>`.
- **`UnifiedChatPanelConnector.tsx`** — a start/join click opens the call only when nothing rotated.

## Security effect vs today

| Case | Today | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Matrix token stolen by a page script | valid ≤ 48 h | ≤ 48 h, usually ≤ 40 h (logged out at rotation) |
| Bus-minted token | ≤ 48 h per mint | unchanged |
| Stolen Alkemio session cookie | 30 d incl. chat | unchanged |
| Live devices per browser | 1 + expired leftovers | 1 (except R-RT-7) |

- 2026-11-09 — HG-1(b) **declined**: minted sessions stay non-refreshable.
- 2026-11-10 — HG-RT-1 **accepted**: rotation only at call start/accept.

Built on the **non-091 path** (`tokenRefresh.ts` absent on `develop`). ## What and why

Voice messages sent from Element now play inline in Alkemio chat instead of showing as a generic file chip that takes several clicks to hear.

Element sends a voice message as an `m.audio` event with the MSC3245 voice marker (`org.matrix.msc3245.voice`) and MSC1767 audio metadata (`org.matrix.msc1767.audio`: `duration`, `waveform`). The web client received these events but read none of those fields. This is **run 1** of workspace#100-chat-voice-messages: client-web playback only. Fixes alkem-io/client-web#10588

Related: alkem-io/client-web#5581 (page/journey titles; the callout dialog was outside its scope, so this is an uncovered path, not a regression)

## Root cause
`document.title` has one owner, `src/core/routing/documentTitle.ts`. It composes `${prefix}${override ?? base}`. The only writer of `base` is `usePageTitle`, and that hook is called only at page/layout level. Nothing in the callout dialog path wrote a title. When a callout detail dialog was open, including on its own `…/collaboration/<calloutNameId>` URL, the tab kept the Space/Subspace title.

## Fix
- `documentTitle.ts` gets a dialog layer: `claimDialogTitle(text)` returns a release function. The newest open claim is shown. The composition is now `${prefix}${override ?? dialogTitle ?? base}`:
  - the unread-badge `override` still wins, exactly as it wins over `base`;
  - the badge `prefix` still composes on top;
  - `base` is never overwritten, so releasing every claim shows the current page title without the page re-running its effect.
- `usePageTitle.ts`: the `<title> | Alkemio` composition (`pages.titles.separator` / `pages.titles.alkemio`) moves into `useComposedTitle`, so pages and dialogs build the string the same way. `usePageTitle` behaves the same as before (its existing tests pass unchanged).
- New `useDialogTitle(title, enabled)`. While `enabled` it holds a claim, and it releases it when `enabled` turns false or the component unmounts.
- `CalloutDetailDialogConnector` calls `useDialogTitle(callout.framing.profile.displayName, open)`. Every opener renders this connector:
  - feed card (`LazyCalloutItem`);
  - callout URL (`CrdSpaceCalloutPage` / `CrdSubspaceCalloutPage` → `CrdCalloutDialogFromUrl` → `CalloutDeeplinkView`);
  - Post Index (`CrdCalloutDialogById` → `CalloutDeeplinkView`).

  The fix is applied once, at that shared owner. The ~25 page call sites are untouched.
- `TaskBoardDialog` calls `useDialogTitle(title, open)`. A Tasks board callout does not open the detail dialog at all, from its feed card (`LazyCalloutItem`) or from its URL (`CalloutDeeplinkView`). It opens the board dialog instead, so that is the second owner. Code review found it.

### Why owned claims and not a single slot
A task's detail dialog opens on top of its board dialog (`elevated`), and both claim the title. With a single slot, closing the task cleared the title while the board was still open. Each claim now releases only itself, and releasing out of order is safe. Within one commit, React runs every passive cleanup before any setup, so swapping one dialog for another never flashes the page title.

## Regression tests
- `src/core/routing/useDialogTitle.test.ts` covers:
  - the singleton layer: dialog title shown, prefix composes, override wins, close restores base, and a base change made while open shows after close;
  - the hook: disabled does nothing; enabled → composed title; disabled or unmount → page title restored; title change followed.

  - nested claims: the board title survives the task dialog closing, and releasing out of order leaves the upper title.

  On the base code it fails, because `claimDialogTitle` / `useDialogTitle` do not exist.
- `src/main/crdPages/space/callout/CalloutDetailDialogConnector.tabTitle.test.tsx` renders the real connector:
  - closed: page title unchanged;
  - open: `Mobile issues tracker | Alkemio`;
  - rerendered closed: page title restored;
  - unread prefix composes, and unmount restores.

  Before the connector change, the open and prefix cases failed (2 of 3 red).
- `src/main/crdPages/space/callout/TaskBoardDialog.tabTitle.test.tsx` renders the real board dialog. ## Summary

Wherever a list of files can be added, users can now pick several files in one selection: a Documents response imports each picked document as its own staged item, the Links & Files dialogs add one row per uploaded file, and every references editor (profiles, space About and community guidelines, templates, innovation packs, posts and callouts) fills the clicked row and appends a row per further file. Up to 25 files are taken per selection; files left out by count, size or type are named in one dismissible notice, and a failed upload is reported once per file instead of one toast each. Save, Publish and template or pack actions are withheld while files are still uploading, only one pick runs at a time, and Discard or a form reset drops uploads that are still running.

## Root cause

alkem-io/client-web#10513: every file input on these surfaces accepted exactly one file per pick, so attaching several documents meant repeating the same dialog flow per file. The workspace spec workspace#094-upload-multiple-documents-files-at-once defines one selection rule, one notice and one bounded upload queue for all of them, and (story decision 10, FR-012) that the client deletes no upload.

## Fix

A shared file selection rule and notice (src/crd/lib/fileSelection, FileSelectionStatus), a silent mode on useReferenceFileUpload that rejects by type and size before any mutation and reports an uploading flag, and a row upload queue (useRowFileUploads) with one commit path for row writes (useRowsCommit), which addresses every row of ReferencesEditor and LinksPrePopulateRows by a client-only ID, so an upload result lands on its own row or nowhere. The Documents add connector imports a batch with per-item status; the Links & Files add and edit connectors use the shared upload hook, create rows under Promise.allSettled and refresh once after all settle, and a partly failed Create keeps only the failed rows, so a retry creates no link twice; LinkUrlAttachFileButton and the client-side deleteDocument cleanup are removed. Every host reads the uploading flag to withhold Save (the settings tabs through one useUploadGate helper), and the profile, About and guidelines editors are remounted on Discard so pending uploads are dropped. New strings are in the CRD namespaces in all six languages. Residual R-8 remains open: abandoned uploads, temporary from the Links & Files dialogs and permanent from a references editor on an existing entity, stay stored with their file name and uploader until alkem-io/server#6737 expires unreferenced documents; multi-file selection raises the per-pick count from 1 to 25. This is a medium residual for the release decision, not accepted by this change.

## Tests

Unit and component tests for the selection rule, the notice, the upload hook's silent mode, the row upload queue and commit path, ReferencesEditor and LinksPrePopulateRows (multi-file placement, late results, unmount, the 25-file cap, type rejections, disabled paperclips while uploading), the Documents add connector batch, the Links & Files add and edit connectors (no deleteDocument on cancel, row removal or replacement; one refresh after all rows settle; failure handling), and every host's Save withholding and Discard behaviour.

This release fixes security issues in how the client decides to use TLS and which servers it takes from the cluster. Some of these fixes change how the client connects: read **BREAKING CHANGES** below before upgrading.

##### BREAKING CHANGES

- Core NATS:
  - **TLS settings now require TLS.** `Options.TLSConfig`, `RootCAsCB` or `TLSCertCB` set directly now act like `Secure()`. Against a server without TLS, the connection fails. Against a server where TLS is optional (`allow_non_tls`, `InProcessServer()`), the client now uses TLS, so the certificate must verify. To connect without TLS, drop the TLS settings ([#​2245](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2245))
  - **`ErrSecureConnWanted` is wrapped.** Compare with `errors.Is(err, nats.ErrSecureConnWanted)`. `==` no longer matches ([#​2245](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2245))
  - **With TLS after INFO, discovered servers come only from the INFO received inside TLS.** The plaintext INFO before the handshake no longer adds servers, and neither does a failed attempt. A TLS client configured with a single server URL therefore:

    - has nothing to fail over to against nats-server before 2.12, until the server sends a later INFO.
    - fails `Connect()` when that server fails it after its INFO, for example at `max_connections` (reported as a TLS handshake error, not the server's reason), or with a certificate that doesn't match a server configured by IP.

    Configure more than one server URL to keep fail-over. For a server configured by IP, set `TLSConfig.ServerName` to a name in its certificate ([#​2245](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats.go/issues/2245))
  - **`SetServerPool()` with a `tls://` URL turns TLS on for the connection**, as it does at `Connect()`. Plaintext servers in that pool can no longer be reached. ##### Added

General

- Account subject mappings, imports, exports and leafnode remote permissions now support the `{{account-hash()}}`, `{{account-hash-import()}}` and `{{account-hash-leaf-remote()}}` subject mapping functions ([#​8670](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8670))
- TLS configuration now supports `verify: optional`, and the command line supports `--tlsverify=optional`, verifying client certificates when provided while allowing clients without certificates ([#​8812](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8812), contributed by [@​macphersonjamie](https://redirect.github.com/macphersonjamie))
- Leafnode connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` ([#​8718](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8718), contributed by [@​stackedbyaradhya](https://redirect.github.com/stackedbyaradhya))
- Gateway connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` ([#​8717](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8717), contributed by [@​stackedbyaradhya](https://redirect.github.com/stackedbyaradhya))
- The command line now supports `-t --test_reload <file>` to check whether a configuration change can be reloaded or requires a restart, returning exit code 3 when a restart is required; embedded servers can use `CheckReload` and `CheckReloadOptions` ([#​8829](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8829))

Monitoring

- Healthz now supports `leaf-remotes-connected=true`, returning an unavailable status until every enabled solicited leafnode remote is connected ([#​8735](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8735), contributed by [@​edjeffreys](https://redirect.github.com/edjeffreys))

##### Improved

General

- Route, gateway and leafnode connection logs now include remote destinations ([#​8755](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8755))
- Account import failures now log their reasons at error level ([#​8771](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8771))
- Gateway connections now validate protocol operations consistently with route connections ([#​8780](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8780))

JetStream

- Filestore subject matching and pending message calculations now avoid unnecessary scans and stop earlier when matches are found ([#​8784](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8784), [#​8803](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8803), [#​8806](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8806), [#​8808](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8808), [#​8813](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8813))

##### Fixed

General

- Account updates no longer unnecessarily recheck importers when export revocations have not changed ([#​8851](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8851))

JetStream

- JetStream no longer shuts down prematurely during server shutdown or lame duck mode ([#​8708](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8708), contributed by [@​yousefissa](https://redirect.github.com/yousefissa))
- Raft meta-group setup failures now stop the write-ahead log instead of leaking it ([#​8722](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8722), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))

- Filestore `MultiLastSeqs` no longer skips matching subjects ([#​8769](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8769))
- Fixed a directory creation race when enabling account storage concurrently with stream creation ([#​8767](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8767), contributed by [@​ansh0014](https://redirect.github.com/ansh0014))
- Deleting a stream no longer races with account directory cleanup ([#​8774](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8774), contributed by [@​ansh0014](https://redirect.github.com/ansh0014))
- Sources no longer discard the remainder of a batch when one sourced message is rejected ([#​8772](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8772))
- Pull requests made through service imports are now removed when the requester loses interest, even while response wildcard interest remains ([#​8797](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8797))
- Consumers no longer deliver while a reset is in flight or report later deliveries in reset responses, and durable mirrors and sources no longer skip messages after a reset or stale delivery ([#​8802](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8802))
- Memory store purge and last-sequence scans are now bounded by the possible sequence range ([#​8815](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8815))

- Filestore recovery failures now return the original error instead of panicking, preserve existing stream data and avoid incorrect storage accounting ([#​8844](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8844), contributed by [@​rleungx](https://redirect.github.com/rleungx))

Leafnodes

Routes

- Routes without pooling now validate the route pool index correctly ([#​8782](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8782))

MQTT

The next release in one PR. It brings two features to `develop`. Each one's spec, plan, contracts and tasks are in `specs/`.

| Feature | What it does | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **026 — Space access gate** | Use of an app depends on the person's **role** on designated Alkemio Spaces. Production gates only the VNG monitor, by [`programmagroei`](https://alkem.io/programmagroei) | `specs/026-space-access-gate/`, previously #164 |
| **027 — VNG admin area** | The monitor gets its own list of Spaces, a settings area for managers, and no Space selection for viewers | `specs/027-vng-admin-area/`, previously #168 |

> 027 builds on 026 and **changes one of its rules**. **Manage** is now `ADMIN` on one of the app's separate **admin Spaces** (`access.vng_admin`, default `programmagroei`), even without `MEMBER`. 026's "MEMBER + ADMIN on the same Space" rule is gone.

## What changes for people

- **Signed out:** the sign-in screen lists the Spaces whose members can use the monitor, with links.
- **No access:** a no-access screen lists those Spaces, with **Opnieuw controleren**. "Could not verify" (Alkemio slow or unreachable) is a separate screen; it fails closed and is never held. A refusal mid-session switches to it, with no toast and no sign-in loop.
- **Viewers (VNG):**
  - No Space selection: no selection column or drawer, no hub picker, no narrowing. The monitor always reports on the Spaces its managers chose.
  - Header:
    - **In deze monitor** opens a list of those Spaces. It flags any Space missing from your own data (usually: no read rights) and says who has access.
    - **GemeenteDelers meenemen** is a switch that shows a count when it is on.
    - Refresh.
  - The yellow banner stays and now also says which Spaces' members have access. The user menu shows your role ("Gebruiker" or "Beheerder van de monitor") and the same Spaces.
- **Monitor managers:** a settings button opens `/admin`, over the dashboard, so coming back keeps your tab and data. It has four sections:
  - who can use the monitor;
  - **Spaces in the monitor**: view and edit, with a pending diff and a "someone else saved" dialog; additions are limited to top-level Spaces you can read;
  - **classifications of one initiative**, written to Alkemio when you may update that Space;
  - the **GemeenteDelers source**.
- **Explorer and GovTech:** explicitly ungated, with unchanged behaviour. GovTech keeps hub selection.
- **Dutch copy:** "je", "Space", "Inloggen/Uitloggen".

## How it works

- **One access module, `server/src/access/`**
  - Every app must declare `access.<app>`: its viewer Spaces, or `none`. A missing or invalid value stops start-up.
  - **Roles, not privileges.** READ on a public Space is granted to everyone.
  - Enforced before every router with a 403 `ACCESS_DENIED`, distinct from 401. A request belongs to its listener's app **plus any app it names**, which closes the path to `/api/vng/*` through the Explorer's port.
  - The decision is made once per session per app (`access_decisions`, keyed by both Space sets). `requireAccess({ fresh: true })` re-checks with Alkemio before every admin write.
  - New public endpoint `GET /api/auth/access/spaces`. `/me` returns `access.viewerSpaces`.
- **Monitor settings, `server/src/settings/`**
  - Their own tables in the existing single SQLite file. Cache operations never touch them.
  - Seeded once from `monitor-settings.seed.json`, which equals today's `vih-test` hub (23 Spaces).
  - Saves carry a revision (a stale save gets 409). Change history is append-only.
  - A daily backup copies only the settings tables, and `node dist/settings/restore-cli.js` restores them.
- **Scope and admin API**
  - VNG reads `GET /api/vng/scope` (SQLite only) instead of a hub.
  - `/api/vng/admin/*` runs with the manager's own token. It includes the first mutation document in the repo, `UpdateClassificationSelection`.
- **Database:** new tables `access_decisions`, `settings_meta`, `settings_state`, `included_spaces`, `settings_changes`, `classification_changes`. No `CACHE_MAINTENANCE_VERSION` bump.
- **Constitution:** 4.3.2.
- **New configuration:**
  - `VNG_ADMIN_GATE`, `VNG_ACCESS_GATE_NAMES`, `SETTINGS_BACKUP_DIR`, `SETTINGS_BACKUP_KEEP`.
  - `VNG_ACCESS_GATE=none` now also needs `VNG_ADMIN_GATE=` (empty).
- **Dev:** each SPA proxies to its own listener: VNG on :4101, GovTech on :4102.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Operational guarantees, handled separately:** a persistent volume, a backup location that survives losing it, and a restore drill.
- **Accessibility follow-up:** keyboard navigation inside the popovers, and real modal dialogs in the admin area. The easy fixes are included.
- **Known, unrelated failure:** `tests/vng-initiatives-export.spec.mjs` header test already fails on `develop`. It expects no Groeifase/TRL columns.

## Test plan

- [x] Server: 489 tests, `tsc` clean. Covers:
  - the policy and sets logic, the per-Space checks, the probe and the decision store;
  - real-HTTP gating, including the Explorer-port path, and 401/403 on every admin route;
  - the settings store, seed, backup/restore and isolation from the cache;
  - GemeenteDelers counts matching the browser summary.
- [x] VNG unit tests (199). Builds pass for VNG, GovTech and Explorer.
- [x] Playwright VNG specs: 61, including `vng-access-gate`, `vng-admin-area`, and `mobile-navigation` at 390, 820 and 1440 px.
- [x] Built server against a temporary DB: seeds 23 Spaces and writes a backup. A second start doesn't re-seed, and the restore CLI works.
- [ ] End-to-end sign-in with a real member and a real non-member account (026 quickstart §3).
- [ ] T058: confirm with two accounts that `UPDATE` on `about.authorization.myPrivileges` predicts whether a classification save succeeds.
- [ ] T070: the 027 manual scenario run (quickstart §3).

## What

`ensureAuthorizationPolicies` — a new lib step wired into server-api global setup after `ensureHarnessAdminRoles` — issues `authorizationPolicyResetAll` as the harness admin, waits for the server's asynchronous reset task, then for a space read to settle. Governed by `AUTH_POLICY_RESET_ON_SETUP`:

| value | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `off` (default) | never resets — nothing changes for the nightly |
| `always` | resets unconditionally, e.g. right after a server upgrade that changed authorization rules |
| `auto` | resets only when the admin is denied a space read |

`AUTH_POLICY_RESET_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 300 s) bounds the wait. The step runs after the role grant on purpose: a bootstrap admin without `PLATFORM_CONTENT_FULL_ACCESS` is denied `Space.settings` for want of the role, not of a reset.

## Why

A server upgrade that changes the authorization rule set leaves every stored policy as it was until the reset rewrites it. Until now that was a manual mutation someone had to remember (the server's `dev-seed-roles` compose service prints it as its last line). With this it is one env var.

## Verification

- Live on a locally seeded stack (server 0.171.0): `auto` detected the denied read, issued the reset, the task completed 61/61 while the auth-reset worker scaled 0→3→0, and the settle window then correctly reported the admin still denied — because it lacked the content role, which `ensureHarnessAdminRoles` grants. That finding is why the default is `off` and the probe runs after the grant; it is recorded in `docs/qa-knowledge/harness.md` together with the seeded-admin vs harness password split that actually blocks local runs.
- `off` verified as a no-op.
- `pnpm -C lib run lint` (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only), `pnpm -C lib run build`, server-api `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## What

The **W1 server behaviour knowledge base** for the rebuild: 34 tables of behaviour rules under `docs/qa/server-rebuild/knowledge/`, plus the generated access matrix. Together they state what today's server guarantees, why, for whom, and how much of it is proven — the oracle the new core is checked against and the gaps list the new net is built from.

Docs only. Base `develop`. Ten signed commits.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tables | 34 — 23 of the 25 legacy test areas (`platform-roles` and `storage` are collapsed into the access matrix) + 11 catalogue features with no legacy test folder |
| Rules | 1,119 |
| Findings (sources disagree or likely defect) | 322 |
| Access matrix | 237 resources × 42 roles × 18 settings variants; 2,631 legacy cases mapped to cells, 11 cross-check findings |
| Server | `develop` @ `eeecf9ddb` (Release/79; authorization builders identical to `v0.170.2` on acceptance) |

## Method — three sources per area

Each table is drawn from three sources with different jobs, so a table cannot inherit a hole the legacy suite had:

1. **Server code + GraphQL schema** give the universe of behaviours (enums, seeds, rules, builders).
2. **The legacy server-api suite** gives the proof: a rule with a green case is *proven*; a rule the code states and no case asserts is *untested* and goes to the gaps.
3. **Specs, ADRs and issues** give the why. Where none exists the row is *unknown-why* and a person fills it.

Where the three disagree the disagreement is a numbered **finding**, never resolved towards the code. Every table has a **who-may** role × action block drawn from the matrix, a constants table with a "product must rule?" column (the rebaseline candidates), the untested rules as its gaps list, and an **open questions** section for what the sources could not settle. The headline findings of every table were spot-checked against the server code; the few claims that could not be located by name are marked as such in the tracker rows.

The first table was extracted from the tests alone and carried 6 of 16 entitlement types, 2 of 11 plans and 2 of 4 feature roles; the method change (`plan.md` § W1) came from that.

## Files

- `knowledge/<area>.md` × 34 — one per area or catalogue feature. Each opens with a one-line **review load** (findings · unknown-why · untested · constants · open questions).
- `knowledge/REVIEW-GUIDE.md` — the seven steps the signing person does with a table; the five places that carry their signature.
- `knowledge/access-matrix.md` + `.json`, `access-matrix-crosscheck.md` + `.json`, `_tools/access/` — the generated oracle, its cross-check against acceptance data and the two largest suites, and the generator.
- `plan.md` § W1 — goal, status values, the three-source method, the who-may block.
- `README.md` (tracker) — W1 progress by area and by catalogue feature, open items, log.

## What to look at first

One ruling closes several tables where noted.

- **Any visitor can read any account's licence, limits, usage and hosted resources** (entitlements F-5, account F-1, innovation-pack F-2).
- **F1 — every document in a space's direct storage bucket is readable without signing in**, whatever the privacy (access matrix; 296 files on acceptance).
- **Push subscriptions accept and POST to any endpoint**, internal addresses included; re-subscribing re-binds an endpoint to another user (push-notifications).
- **Renaming an innovation-flow state sets the callout re-tag in memory and skips the save** (innovation-flow; needs a live probe).
- **Summoning a virtual contributor in a room has no authorization call** (vc-knowledge-base).
- **The `task`/`tasks` queries carry no guard** (admin-operations).
- **A private space's community guidelines are world-readable** by unconditional grant (community-guidelines).
- **`transferVirtualContributorToAccount` is declared as returning `InnovationPack!`** (account).
- **Search returns private top-level spaces to everyone** by design comment; `last` pagination without a cursor returns the first page (search, pagination).
- **Organisations are created with no owner; `requiresEntryRole` is enforced nowhere** (contributor-management, roleset).
- **The room row is removed before the Matrix delete; nobody holds DELETE on a conversation** (communications).
- **The free tier is never issued; the plus trial's expiry is never evaluated** (entitlements).

## How this is reviewed

Per `knowledge/REVIEW-GUIDE.md`: the QA lead signs the why column, decides each finding (file / record as rule / drop), ticks the constants product must rule on, and answers or routes the open questions. Then one product/CTO pass over all findings and ticked constants, and the ticked rows become the rebaseline register (W1 output a). The tracker's open item 3 carries this.

## Not done / caveats

- Nothing is signed by the lead yet; nothing was filed in GitHub; no database was written.
- Three claims could not be located by name and are marked in their tracker rows: the callout post-created push ordering, the collabora rename validator, the `platform.settings` guard. Two more rest on an open issue rather than a line: the template memo with no owner (server#6682), the guest-enabled whiteboard ignoring privacy.
- Sibling clones used for context are behind: notifications (2026-08-05), matrix-adapter (2026-07-21), the engines (2026-07/08); `assistant-service` and `wopi-service` are not local. Each table's open questions say so.
- Several workspace specs exist only on `agents-hq@origin/main`; citations carry that prefix until the local clone is pulled.
- Data-dependent matrix cells are modelled on one representative and marked `data-dependent` in the JSON.

The forge run's Phase-V acceptance walks were driven ad-hoc and **persisted no specs** — its own ledger recorded *"Emitted @forge-acceptance specs: none persisted … the durable-spec follow-up can ride the test-suites flow."* This is that follow-up.

## Coverage — 13 cases, 7 files

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|
| CA-01 | three provider rows *Not connected* + Connect, read-only credential rows, no identity leakage |
| CA-02 | credential rows route via in-page anchors to the password/passkey cards, no inline mutation |
| CA-05 | a password error stays inside the password card (does not echo into the section) |
| CA-06 | owner-only: a platform admin on another user's security URL is redirected, no settings flow created |
| CA-04 | fail-closed when the settings flow is unreadable — explicit error + retry, **zero** provider rows; retry recovers in place |
| CA-03 / CA-07 | last-method lock shows a focusable `aria-disabled` Disconnect carrying its reason; curing the lock flips the same row to enabled |

Live dev stack throughout; Kratos settings-flow **reads** are mocked only where a state cannot be provoked deterministically (locked rows, unreadable flow, completed round-trips). All URLs resolve at runtime from each persona's own profile URL — never a hardcoded `/user/<slug>`.

## Harness changes these depend on

- **`authenticated-session.fixture.ts`** — persona sessions are validated against Kratos `whoami` before reuse, and gain `maxSessionAgeSeconds`. Kratos gates privileged self-service operations behind `privileged_session_max_age` (15m); a live-but-stale cached session makes a privileged submit redirect to a re-auth screen instead of returning the expected settings-flow response. Specs doing privileged work now re-mint rather than mis-assert.
- **`config/global-setup.ts`** — provision personas through the Kratos **admin** API when `KRATOS_ADMIN_URL` is reachable (deterministic; no HIBP/self-service policy; a reset Kratos store heals on the next run instead of timing out every login), falling back to self-service registration otherwise. Then warm every persona's storage state **serially, before any worker exists** — concurrent cold logins were blowing the 30s budget as `Test timeout … exceeded while setting up storageState`. Warm-up failures are deliberately non-fatal so only the affected specs go red, attributably.
- **`getRecoveryLink(recipientEmail?)`** — the MailSlurper inbox is shared. An unfiltered subject match could open **another suite's** recovery mail and complete recovery against it, silently resetting that persona's harness credential for the rest of the run. `authentication-password-recovery.spec.ts` updated to pass its own address.

- `tsc --noEmit` clean — `client-web` and `lib`
- `eslint` clean on every new/changed file

| Run | Workers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (3.1m) |
| 2 | 2 | 15 passed, 1 failed (1.9m) |
| 3 | 1 | 15 passed, 1 failed (2.2m) |

The 15 are stable and fast (1.5-4.7s each) across all three runs — every case that exercises Connected Accounts itself is green.

### The one failure is NOT a test defect and NOT 051

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Two defects, both on the **login/OIDC bootstrap** — a surface 051 does not touch:

1. The login flow is created **twice** in one cold sign-in; the SPA then fetches the flow id from the URL while the anti-CSRF cookie has moved on, and Kratos rejects it with `security_csrf_violation`.
2. On that 403 the SPA **hangs indefinitely** on "Preparing secure sign-in…" — no error surfaced, no retry, no recovery.

Reproduction rate on this stack was high but not total (one fresh context in an early batch of three succeeded; a later batch of four failed 4/4), which is what made CA-41 look flaky before the cause was isolated.

This is the same *class* of bug the 051 review already fixed on the settings page ("settings flow created before `profileUrl` resolved — double flow creation, lost `return_to`"); this is the login page's version of it, and it is pre-existing.

**CA-41 is a regression guard for pre-existing recovery behaviour**, so it never reaches the 051 code under test. It should not gate this PR's assessment of the feature, but it does need a decision: fix the login bootstrap, or make CA-41 tolerate a stale flow id.

The 8 off-site OAuth round-trips (LinkedIn/Microsoft/GitHub) from the original walk stay out of automation; the provider hop is asserted up to the redirect only.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.
